- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.00), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% from prior peak) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 5–10% downward bias for the first 3–5 days of forecast horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (±15% from 14-day moving average); cap forecast within ±10% of recent 7-day average unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.67+), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days to avoid overcorrection.
